Population increased in Middlesbrough

The estimated population of Middlesbrough in 2024 was 156,161 usual residents, a rise of 1.6% since 2023.

This meant that Middlesbrough's rate of population change placed it among the 20 percent fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Middlesbrough increased by 8.5%.

Over this slightly longer period, Middlesbrough was also among the 10% fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Middlesbrough

The average (median) age stayed at 36.3 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Middlesbrough has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Middlesbrough is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Middlesbrough's population of 156,161 usual residents was made up of:

  • 31,762 people aged 0 to 15 years, (20.3%)
  • 98,418 people aged 16 to 64 years, (63%)
  • 25,981 people aged 65 years and over, (16.6%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Middlesbrough has a slightly lower proportion of people aged 65 years and over (16.6% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Middlesbrough, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Middlesbrough
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Middlesbrough, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 325 people (0.2%). In total, there were 1,859 births and 1,534 deaths in Middlesbrough.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 3,483 (-2.3%). There were 7,589 people entering the area and 11,072 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Middlesbrough's population of 5,673 (3.7%) as a result of 7,685 people entering the area and 2,012 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Middlesbrough was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Middlesbrough in mid-2023 is 153,639.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 825 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 164 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 989 people.
